title: Spanakopita
subtitle: Greek spinach and feta filo pie
excerpt: Layers of buttered filo pastry filled with a mixture of wilted spinach, crumbled feta, eggs, and dill. Baked until shatteringly crisp on top and soft within. The essential Greek savory pie.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spanakopita (spinach pie) is one of Greece's best-known dishes, served across the country in bakeries, cafes, and home kitchens. Fyllo (filo) pastry is essential: no other pastry gives the same shattering crispness. Fresh filo sheets should be kept under a damp cloth while working to prevent them drying out. The filling must be very dry before it goes into the pastry: any excess moisture from the spinach will make the base soggy. Squeeze the wilted spinach hard in a clean cloth.

content.text: Squeeze every drop of moisture from the spinach: wet filling makes soggy pastry. Keep unused filo under a damp tea towel while you work: it dries out in seconds. Brush each filo sheet with melted butter before layering. The top layer should be generously buttered and scored before baking so it does not shatter when cut.
Wilt the spinach in a large pan with the olive oil over high heat. Transfer to a colander and leave to cool. Once cool, squeeze out as much liquid as possible in a clean cloth.
Combine the squeezed spinach, feta, beaten eggs, dill, spring onion, nutmeg, and pepper in a bowl. Mix well.

Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Butter a 30 x 20 cm baking dish. Lay half the filo sheets in the base, brushing each with melted butter and letting the edges overhang. Add the filling. Fold the overhanging edges in. Lay the remaining filo sheets on top, brushing each with butter. Score the top layer into portions with a sharp knife.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Cool for 10 minutes before cutting along the scored lines.
